title: Inefficient Multidimensional Array Access (Cache-Unfriendly Stride)
pattern: Traversing a multidimensional array where the innermost loop advances the slow-moving index (columns in row-major languages, or rows in column-major languages).
why_bad: It breaks spatial locality, causing the CPU to miss the cache on nearly every access as it fetches entire cache lines but reads only single elements across huge strides.
detection: Nested loops where the array subscripts are indexed in an order opposite to the language's physical memory layout (e.g., C/C++/Java/Rust column-first loops).
counterexample: The matrix is extremely small and fits entirely in L1 cache. `Contextual`.
fix: Re-order the nested loop headers so that the innermost loop iterates across contiguous memory (row-by-row in row-major).
source: *Code Complete*, Chapter 26, "Looping" (p. 187) and *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 3, "Measuring Cache Line Size" (p. 39 / p. 220).
